title: Amnon Shashua and Ziv Aviram founded Mobileye: a single camera in the car that detects danger on the road

trailer.text: Prof. Amnon Shashua, a researcher at the Hebrew University, founded Mobileye, an Israeli company for driver-assistance systems, in 1999.
While the industry assumed that radar or two cameras would be needed, Shashua showed that a wealth of information could be extracted from the image of a single camera.
A camera at the front of the vehicle captures the road, and a computer vision system analyzes lanes, vehicles, pedestrians, traffic signs and other hazards in real time.
Intel acquired the company in 2017 for $15.3 billion, and as of July 2026 more than 250 million vehicles had been produced with its technology.

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: More than 250 million vehicles, in more than 1,400 models (July 2026)

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement to Shashua, 2023

stations.title: Before: expensive radar, and only in luxury cars

paragraphs.text: When Mobileye was founded, the prevailing belief in the industry was that expensive radar sensors were necessary to perform the safety functions.
According to Aviram, a vision system was then considered unreliable technology.
The expensive and cumbersome equipment of earlier assistance systems restricted their use to luxury vehicles.
People are killed and injured on the world's roads every year, and the sources give different numbers.
Aviram said that drivers are responsible for 93% of accidents.
According to a 2016 article, 35,000 people have been killed in road accidents in Israel since the founding of the state, 50% more than those who fell in wars and terrorism.
The founders wanted to increase road safety by helping to prevent collisions, not only by reducing the severity of injuries.

stations.title: A question from a car maker, and a motorbike trip in the Negev

paragraphs.text: Shashua served in the IDF Armored Corps, and his service included the First Lebanon War.
Afterwards, in 1982, he began studying at Tel Aviv University.
He carried out his academic research at the Hebrew University.
According to the Jerusalem Post, at a conference in late 1998 a car maker asked him whether two cameras could identify the location of a vehicle.
According to ynet, in 1999 Shashua was invited to a meeting with automotive industry executives in Japan.
According to Aviram, the Japanese company gave Shashua 250 thousand dollars to develop a proof of concept.
The decision to found the company was made when Shashua and Aviram were on a motorbike trip in the Negev.
Aviram took on operations, finance and investor relations, and Shashua took on technology, R&D and the strategic vision.
With the help of a broker, Aviram approached 100 wealthy people to raise initial money.
Aviram said that they took a student, built a computer and presented a concept to the Japanese.
According to Mobileye, Shashua proved that automatic emergency braking and other perception tasks could also be performed with a single camera.
According to the Times of Israel, the single-lens camera was inspired by human vision, which uses one eye for depth perception.
How does it work? A camera at the front of the vehicle captures the road.
A computer vision system analyzes lanes, vehicles, pedestrians, traffic signs and other hazards in real time.
Algorithms in the hardware compare changes in the size and position of nearby objects every 27 milliseconds, and calculate their speed and trajectory.
According to the European Patent Office, Shashua and his team combined a single lens and artificial intelligence to detect hazards in real time.

stations.title: Their own chip, and the first contracts

paragraphs.text: According to Mobileye, the decision to design its own chip was considered radical and even risky, but the leadership saw it as essential.
Aviram said that experts told them to give up the "stupidity" of developing their own chip.
The first EyeQ1 chip, running on a 180 nanometer process, was sampled in 2004.
Aviram explained that the company chose to sell the chip to parts suppliers such as Delphi and Magna, who would build a system around it for car makers.
In 2007 the company received an investment of $130 million from Goldman Sachs.
According to Aviram, that same year the first manufacturing agreements were signed, with General Motors, Volvo and BMW.

Mobileye's first breakthrough came when a car manufacturer asked for a demonstration of a single-camera lane detection system; the company also included object detection in the demonstration, and the clients saw a single-camera system detecting various objects, something considered impossible until then.
Following that demonstration, as part of the company's first breakthrough, the clients stopped their bid for ADAS systems and began working with Mobileye.
According to an analyst, single-camera technology is cheaper and allows quick and easy installation.
According to the Weizmann Institute, the products cost about $100–150 for car manufacturers and $600–1,000 for private car owners.

stations.title: From a few vehicles to a quarter of a billion

paragraphs.text: Aviram said that in 2014 regulators in Europe required car manufacturers to have emergency braking as a condition for a high safety rating.
According to Shashua, it is the regulator who dictates the penetration of the systems, by setting rules whereby every new vehicle must be equipped with them.

According to a 2016 article, a regulation of Israel's Ministry of Transportation requires the device to be installed in every heavy vehicle over 3.5 tons as of November 1, and the article does not state the year.
According to insurance company data audited by an actuary, the device cuts accidents by half.
According to the company's description in Intel's announcement, its technology reduces the risks of accidents and saves lives.
By 2016–2017 Mobileye systems were already in millions of vehicles, and the sources give different numbers.
There are also several versions of the company's market share.
According to Mobileye, as of March 2023 more than 130 million vehicles had been built with its technology.
As of July 2026, more than 250 million vehicles had been produced with EyeQ technology, in more than 1,400 models.

stations.title: An IPO, Intel, and the headquarters stays in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: In August 2014 Mobileye raised $890 million in an IPO on the New York Stock Exchange.
According to ynet, it was the largest IPO ever by an Israeli company up to that time.
According to the Times of Israel, revenue in 2016 was $358 million.
In March 2017 Intel announced that it would acquire all of Mobileye's shares for $63.54 per share, at an equity value of approximately $15.3 billion.
The price was a 35 percent premium to the company's market value.
It was the largest exit in the history of Israeli high-tech at the time.
According to Globes, each of the founders held about 7% of the company and was expected to receive about a billion dollars in cash.
After the acquisition Aviram stepped down, Shashua became CEO, and the headquarters and R&D center remained in Jerusalem.
According to Intel's announcement, the combined organization would be based in Israel and led by Shashua.
In March 2017 the company had over 750 employees, and later over 2,500 full-time employees.
Revenue rose from just over 350 million dollars at the end of 2016 to almost a billion dollars at the end of 2020.
Mobileye, BMW and Intel announced that they would together put 40 autonomous vehicles on roads in the US and Europe.
According to ynet, in June 2026 Mobileye announced plans to operate its own robotaxi service in the United States beginning in 2027.

stations.title: Recognition, and the people behind the camera

paragraphs.text: In September 2016 Globes named Mobileye the Israeli company of the decade.
Globes described Shashua and Aviram as two of the most successful Israeli technology entrepreneurs of all time.
On Independence Day 2017, Shashua was chosen to light a torch at the national ceremony on Mt. Herzl.
Shashua and his team were finalists for the European Patent Office's European Inventor Award 2019.
In 2022 Shashua received the Mobility Innovator Award from the Automotive Hall of Fame.
On March 22, 2023, the Ministry of Education named Shashua the recipient of the Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement.
He was honored for his contribution to the high-tech industry in Israel, his impact on automotive safety and artificial intelligence, and his philanthropy.
Shashua and his family have donated about $60 million to philanthropic causes.
In 2010 Shashua and Aviram founded OrCam, a start-up that operates on the bottom floor of the Mobileye building in Har Hotzvim.

stations.title: What did not succeed, and what threatens

paragraphs.text: Before Mobileye, Shashua had a start-up called CogniTens.
It was sold in 2007 to Hexagon for $20 million, less than had been invested in it.
According to the Times of Israel, the company is expected to face challenges, especially from companies like Google that are developing disruptive technologies in the field.
According to an analyst, without Intel Mobileye could have faced increasing competition from Nvidia, Google and others.

claims.quote: it controls an 80 percent share of the single-camera ADAS market

claims.text: לפי מובילאיי, יותר מ-130 מיליון כלי רכב נבנו עם טכנולוגיית החברה.
claims.quote: To date, more than 130 million vehicles worldwide have been built with Mobileye technology inside.

claims.text: באוגוסט 2014 גייסה מובילאיי 890 מיליון דולר בהנפקה.
claims.quote: The pinnacle came in August 2014 when Mobileye raised an unprecedented $890m.

claims.text: ב-2014 מובילאיי הונפקה בבורסת ניו יורק, בהנפקה הגדולה אי פעם של חברה ישראלית עד אז, לפי ynet.
claims.quote: In 2014, Mobileye went public on the New York Stock Exchange in what was then the largest IPO ever by an Israeli company.

claims.text: לפי הטיימס אוף ישראל, ההכנסות ב-2016 היו 358 מיליון דולר והרווח עלה ל-108 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Mobileye’s revenue in 2016 totaled $358 million, up from $241 million a year earlier. Profits rose to $108 million from $68 million.

claims.text: מחיר הרכישה היה פרמיה של 35 אחוז על שווי השוק של מובילאיי.
claims.quote: at a price that represented 35 percent premium to the market value of Mobileye

claims.text: לפי גלובס, כל אחד מהמייסדים מחזיק בכ-7% מהחברה וצפוי לקבל כמיליארד דולר במזומן.
claims.quote: Each of them holds about 7% of the company (including options, which are now in the money) which means that each will receive about $1 billion cash.

claims.text: הארגון המשותף ימוקם בישראל בראשות פרופ' אמנון שעשוע, ממייסדי מובילאיי.
claims.quote: will be headquartered in Israel and led by Prof. Amnon Shashua, Mobileye’s Co-Founder, Chairman and CTO.

claims.text: במרץ 2017 היו במובילאיי מעל 750 עובדים, ובהמשך מעל 2,500 עובדים במשרה מלאה.
claims.quote: In March 2017, Mobileye had over 750 employees whereas today there are over 2500 employees in a full time capacity.

claims.text: ההכנסות עלו מקצת יותר מ-350 מיליון דולר בסוף 2016 לכמעט מיליארד דולר בסוף 2020.
claims.quote: Revenue as well went from just over $350 million at the end of 2016, to close to $1B at the end of 2020

claims.text: מובילאיי, BMW ואינטל הודיעו שיעלו יחד 40 כלי רכב אוטונומיים לכבישי ארה"ב ואירופה.
claims.quote: Mobileye, BMW and Intel announced they would together put 40 self-driven cars on US and European roads later this year.

claims.text: ב-yנט נמסר שבחודש יוני הודיעה מובילאיי על תוכניות להפעיל שירות רובוטקסי משלה בארצות הברית החל מ-2027.
claims.quote: In June, Mobileye took another step, announcing plans to operate its own robotaxi service in the United States beginning in 2027

claims.text: בספטמבר 2016 גלובס בחר במובילאיי כחברה הישראלית של העשור.
claims.quote: In September 2016, Mobileye was named by "Globes" Israeli company of the decade.

claims.text: גלובס תיאר את שעשוע ואבירם כשניים מיזמי הטכנולוגיה הישראלים המצליחים ביותר בכל הזמנים.
claims.quote: They are two of the most successful Israeli entrepreneurs of all time.

claims.text: ביום העצמאות 2017 שעשוע נבחר להדליק משואה בטקס הממלכתי בהר הרצל.
claims.quote: On Israeli Independence Day 2017, Shashua was chosen for one of the highest honors in Israeli society, to light a torch at the national ceremony on Mt. Herzl.

claims.text: שעשוע וצוותו היו מועמדים לגמר פרס הממציא האירופי 2019 של הרשות האירופית לפטנטים.
claims.quote: Shashua and his team from Mobileye were finalists in the European Inventor Awards of 2019, awarded by the European Patent Office.

claims.text: ב-2022 שעשוע קיבל את פרס Mobility Innovator מהיכל התהילה של הרכב.
claims.quote: Shashua received the Mobility Innovator Award from the Automotive Hall of Fame

claims.text: שעשוע זכה על תרומתו לתעשיית ההייטק בישראל, להשפעתו על בטיחות הרכב ובינה מלאכותית ולפילנתרופיה.
claims.quote: Shashua was honored for his groundbreaking contributions to the tech industry in Israel, his global impact on automotive safety and applied artificial intelligence, and his philanthropy.

claims.text: שעשוע ומשפחתו תרמו כ-60 מיליון דולר למטרות פילנתרופיות.
claims.quote: To date, he and his family have donated about $60 million to philanthropic causes, including scholarships at TAU.

claims.text: אורקם, סטארט-אפ שהוקם ב-2010 על ידי שעשוע ואבירם, פועל בקומה התחתונה של בניין מובילאיי בהר חוצבים.
claims.quote: On the bottom floor of Mobileye's building, in Jerusalem's Har Hotzvim, there is a start-up, Orcam, founded in 2010 by Shashua and Aviram.

claims.text: סטארט-אפ קודם של שעשוע, קוגניטנס, נמכר ב-2007 ב-20 מיליון דולר להקסגון, פחות ממה שהושקע בו.
claims.quote: CogniTens developed vision and measurement systems for quality control in the vehicle and aircraft industries, but it was sold in 2007 for $20 million (less than had been invested in it) to Swedish company Hexagon.

claims.text: לפי הטיימס אוף ישראל, צפויים אתגרים, בעיקר מחברות כמו גוגל המפתחות טכנולוגיות משבשות בתחום.
claims.quote: There are challenges ahead, however, especially from companies like Google that are developing disruptive technologies in the field.

claims.text: לפי אנליסט, ללא אינטל מובילאיי הייתה עלולה לעמוד בפני תחרות גוברת מצד אנבידיה, גוגל ואחרות.
claims.quote: Mobileye could have continued on the path it was on, but would have faced steadily increasing competition from Nvidia, Google, and others.

claims.text: אבירם סיפר שאחרי כמעט חצי שנה חזרו ללקוח והציגו לו קונספט ראשוני.
claims.quote: We went back to that customer after almost half a year, and demonstrated an initial concept to him.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, הכנסות 2016 צפויות להסתכם בכ-350 מיליון דולר ורווח של כ-200 מיליון.
claims.quote: whose revenues in 2016 will total about $350 million, generating some $200m.
